title: The visual cliff
why: Capra depth_cue: the web search "visual cliff goat kids depth perception Gibson Walk" (run after "Capra depth perception" and "goat depth perception" returned only general and popular pages) returned the Wikipedia article on the visual cliff and secondary accounts headed "Visual Cliff Experiment (Gibson & Walk, 1960)" and "Gibson & Walk (1960): The Visual Cliff" (Simply Psychology, Cognito, flashcard sites). The visual-cliff test shows whether a young animal avoids an apparent drop, a behavioural measure of depth perception; that goat kids were among the young animals tested is my own recollection, and none of the returned titles shows it. If they were, the article gives a depth_cue row for Capra hircus (depth perception shown behaviourally, cue unnamed). The journal, volume and pages are not given here because no result showed them. Main holds no depth_cue row for a goat; its one bovid row is the sheep (canon-3#4, Nityananda and Read 2017), and the harvest's citation step on that review found 0 works naming Capra. Not opened.

why: Spheniscus acuity_cpd and interreceptor_deg: a schematic eye of the Humboldt penguin, a hit of the harvest queries "Spheniscus vision" and "Spheniscus eye" and a listed candidate for both traits. The stored abstract gives the powers of the lens (100 dioptres) and of the cornea in air (29 dioptres), the eye's myopia in air and its binocular field. A schematic eye gives the posterior nodal distance that turns photoreceptor spacing into an angle (interreceptor_deg), and the paper may estimate the retina's resolving power (acuity_cpd). Main holds no row from it; its field rows for this species come from Martin and Katzir 1999. The harvest also lists the 1987 study of refraction in air and water (10.1098/rspb.1987.0005), the 1984 microspectrophotometric study (10.1016/0042-6989(84)90359-6), the 1985 pigment and oil-droplet study (10.1007/bf00610668), the 1976 study of the flat cornea of the blackfoot penguin (10.1139/z76-151) and the 1990 study of the anterior segment of the Magellanic penguin eye (10.1002/aja.1001890307), whose titles and stored abstracts concern refraction, pigments and the anterior eye and show no acuity. Not opened.

title: Retinal Morphology and Electrophysiology of Two Caprimulgiformes Birds: The Cave-Living and Nocturnal Oilbird (Steatornis caripensis), and the Crepuscularly and Nocturnally Foraging Common Pauraque (Nyctidromus albicollis)
why: Nyctidromus acuity_cpd, interreceptor_deg, cff_hz, lambda_max_nm and spectral_range_nm: a study of the common pauraque's own retina, the first hit of the harvest query "Nyctidromus vision" and a candidate for all five traits. The stored abstract says that electroretinograms were recorded under photopic and scotopic conditions over a wide range of light intensities and that the retinas were then examined histologically, and the harvest's subject index of Brain Behavior and Evolution volume 64 (2004) lists "Common pauraque", "Cone" and "Electroretinogram" at page 19, which I take to be this paper. The histology may give photoreceptor and ganglion-cell densities, from which a receptor spacing (interreceptor_deg) and an anatomical acuity (acuity_cpd) follow; the electroretinograms may include flicker responses (cff_hz); and the cone description may give oil-droplet or pigment classes that bear on the pauraque's spectral range (lambda_max_nm, spectral_range_nm). Main holds no row for the pauraque under these traits (its one pauraque row is the binocular type of Martin 2007). The harvest also lists a 2023 study of the pauraque's cornea (10.1111/ahe.12987), a 2017 Maryland thesis on the evolution of nocturnality in the Strisores (10.13016/m2hq3s10n), a 2009 Cardiff thesis on visual constraints on avian behaviour and a 2023 comparison of eye size across birds (10.3390/birds4030024), which may hold eye or retina data for the pauraque as well. The protocol's web pairs were not run for this genus because the harvest's own studies of the species hold every open trait. Not opened.
